## Intent
Hypothesis: fusing the scatter-reduction render into the particle step eliminates intermediate buffer traffic and can approach the streaming ceiling despite byte-granular framebuffer writes.

## Cache saturation
At death_q=0.01, ns/p falls from 11.898 at N=4000 to 7.845 at N=16000 — overhead amortization at small N, since N=4000 already exceeds the L1d spill point (N≈963) and resides in L2. From N=16000 through N=4000000, cost stays FLAT at ~7.6–7.7 ns/p, with no knee at the L2→DRAM spill (N≈61680). The same shape holds at death_q=0.05 (floor ~8.1–8.2) and death_q=0.25 (floor ~10.3): death rate raises the floor without changing the N-shape. The absence of any cache-spill knee confirms the algorithm is not cache-bandwidth-limited at any N.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.93 GB/s at N=262000, death_q=0.01 — 35.4% of the 25.22 GB/s streaming ceiling. At death_q=0.25 the peak falls to 6.61 GB/s (26.2%). Bandwidth is FLAT across N at every death rate (8.86–8.93 GB/s from N=65000 to N=4000000 at q=0.01), confirming the algorithm is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound. The transition is by death rate, not by N: each increase in churn raises the floor (7.6→8.1→10.3 ns/p), consistent with the `bl _layouts.ML1.data.Data.spawn` call and branchy respawn logic adding per-particle cost. The algorithm never approaches the streaming ceiling at any regime.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized across the components of one particle, not across particles. `ldr q1, [x26]` loads the 4-float position, `ext.16b v3, v1, v2, #0xc` rearranges components, and `fmul.4s`/`fadd.4s` update position in 4-wide lanes; a 2-wide pair (`fmul.2s`/`fadd.2s`) handles velocity. There is one gather: `ld1.s {v2}[1], [x8]` loads a single float from a non-contiguous offset within the particle struct. The framebuffer scatter is entirely scalar: `ldrb`/`add`/`cmp`/`csel`/`strb` sequences (16 strb, 12 ldrb in the histogram) perform byte-granular load-modify-store for each RGB channel with 0xff clamping. These byte stores cannot coalesce or stream, explaining the 35% ceiling plateau. The `bl _layouts.ML1.data.Data.spawn` call at death events explains the death-rate-driven floor increase.

## Verdict
Refuted — the fused scatter-reduction render never exceeds 8.93 GB/s (35% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling) at any N or death rate, because the framebuffer scatter's byte-granular `ldrb`/`strb` stores cannot stream. The flat ns/p across N (7.6 ns/p from N=65000 to N=4000000 at q=0.01) confirms the bottleneck is scatter overhead, not memory bandwidth, and the death-rate-driven floor rise (7.6→10.3 ns/p from q=0.01 to q=0.25) adds spawn-call cost on top.
